## Problem and result

Describe the user-visible problem and the resulting behaviour.

## Validation

List commands actually run, source commit, platform and results. Explain skipped
checks and remaining acceptance gaps. For documentation, check links and source
claims. For code, cover changed behaviour and relevant failure paths.

## Risk and recovery

Describe applicable data, privacy, security, provider and compatibility effects.
Explain rollback or recovery for changes that affect stored data or installation.

## Rights and provenance

- [ ] Commits have DCO sign-off.
- [ ] Consulted sources and exact revisions are listed.
- [ ] Copied, adapted or generated material and its licences are identified.
- [ ] Employment, client or confidentiality restrictions are disclosed.
- [ ] Required contributor assignment is verified privately before merge.
- [ ] Proprietary code has not moved without an approved rights record.
- [ ] Applicable licence text, notices and Corresponding Source are preserved.
- [ ] No credentials, private telemetry or personal data are included.
- [ ] No new automation or publication is introduced without owner authorisation.
